correctness.rationale: The derivative of the mean-zero representer at x is t−1_{t≥x}; direct integration yields the stated Gram kernel. The outer antisymmetric unit vector has Rayleigh value L/2 for every configuration. In the symmetric two-dimensional compression the noncentral corrections are entrywise nonnegative, and some entry is strictly increased unless both midpoint and middle-site offsets vanish. For L≤2a*<1/4 the centered compression is entrywise positive and its upper-left and off-diagonal entries strictly decrease with L. The positive maximizing eigenvector therefore detects every strict correction, proving global sharpness and rigidity. For L>2a* the antisymmetric certificate alone excludes optimality. Direct symbolic computation of the full symmetric-triple Gram characteristic polynomial reproduced the factor λ−a and the cubic condition for the remaining quadratic to vanish at λ=a. At the root in (1/9,1/8) the third eigenvalue is positive and strictly below a; the two stated coefficient vectors span the top eigenspace and their Riesz combinations give all nonzero norming inputs. The ordered-configuration argument includes endpoints and coincident indexed sites. Independent high-precision computation gave squared norm 0.12156132517648428235… and third eigenvalue 0.03643166120435733818… .
residual_risks: The relevant cubic root is the unique root in its stated bracket, not the unique positive algebraic root without a domain restriction. No finite-grid inference is used for optimality.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact balance, full location rigidity and equality eigenspace need the nonperiodic endpoint-dependent Gram structure; they are not inherited from circular formulas or pointwise interpolation optima.

evidence: The periodic H¹ record minimizes the same type of objective but over the circle, with cyclic gaps (t,t,1−2t) and optimum (11+√21)/150. Santin minimizes an interpolation power function for a zero-boundary kernel.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Periodicity imposes f(1)=f(0) and removes the unit derivative direction; at identical interval sites the interval Gram differs from the periodic Gram by the rank-one term with entries (x_i−1/2)(x_j−1/2). Translation invariance is lost. Thus neither optimizing gaps alone nor minimizing inverse-Gram prediction error is an equivalent reformulation of the interval problem.
